feed.title: World News - Breaking international news and headlines | Sky News

articles.title: FIFA to double Women's World Cup prize money - but it doesn't match men's tournament
articles.summary: FIFA plans to double Women's World Cup prize money next year but will not deliver on Gianni Infantino's ambition to match the cash paid out at the men's tournament, Sky News has learnt.

articles.title: Google owner Alphabet suffers its worst-ever day on stock market - as value plunges $500bn
articles.summary: Shares in Google's parent company Alphabet have suffered their worst-ever day on the US stock market, falling more than 12% and knocking around half a trillion dollars off its value.

articles.title: Leaflets promoting clinics in illegal Israeli settlements handed out at London medical recruitment event
articles.summary: Sky News has obtained copies of leaflets promoting medical clinics in illegal Israeli settlements by a company seeking to recruit British Jewish doctors at an event in London

articles.title: Why defeated Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil for Miami - and what comes next
articles.summary: On Wednesday, Flavio Bolsonaro, who last week lost Brazil's presidential election, was seen arriving in the US on a private jet after having fled in the dead of night.

articles.title: Will she stand? Lagarde quits European Central Bank ahead of French election
articles.summary: The French head of the European Central Bank (ECB) is to step down from the role, just months ahead of the troubled country's presidential election.

articles.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles off east coast as tensions with South rise
articles.summary: North Korea has launched ballistic missiles off its east coast into the Sea of Japan, South Korea said on Thursday, as tensions continued to rise between the two countries.

articles.title: Girl injured in wolf attack at wildlife park
articles.summary: An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a wildlife park in Germany.

articles.title: US makes interest rate decision - as Bank of England verdict looms
articles.summary: The Federal Reserve has left interest rates unchanged - despite persistently high inflation and repeated calls from Donald Trump to lower borrowing costs.
